analysis:
This is a documentation-only batch. No source or code changes are visible.

docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head 784-790) adds a statement that a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import builds its destinations directly from host bytes. The import does no device eval or fence, so staging no longer waits on MLX's process-wide evalLock. The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. This is an availability/TTFT behavior claim. It touches the T-041/SEC-035 accepted same-account TTFT oracle only in that restore latency becomes faster and more decoupled from concurrent prefill. That may sharpen the hit/miss timing signal, but it is within the already-accepted kind: cacheSalt account scoping is unchanged.

The new text also places this import outside the WholeMacUnboundedActivity scope (head 776-783). Integration should check CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift. It must confirm that:
- destinations created from host bytes still hold only fully authenticated data (head 720-727: auth before staging);
- scratch charging covers the host-zero source;
- skipping fences cannot expose partially written buffers to another request.
The CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift source is not supplied, which limits coverage.

docs/developer/test.md (head 177-208) documents an opt-in live test, ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests. It uses an isolated ephemeral cache under env -i with explicit env vars and writes a report to an operator-chosen path. That is test tooling, not production attack surface, and no secrets are documented.

No threat-model update is required beyond possibly noting the evalLock-free import path under T-041(e) transient staging RAM. The remaining date-line changes are trivial.
